tips.title: Airbrushing Vallejo Model Air vs Model Color
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is ready-to-spray, use as-is or thin 10% with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for better flow. Model Color needs thinning; mix 1:1 with thinner. Add 2 drops Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops paint for fine nozzle setups. Airbrush at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure for Model Air, 1.0-1.5 bar for Model Color. Test on white paper, adjust pressure/flow improver as needed.

tips.title: Base Coating with Vallejo Model Color
tips.text: Shake Vallejo Model Color well before use. Apply 2-3 light coats, letting each dry for 5 minutes. Spray at 1.0-1.5 bar pressure. For best adhesion, use Vallejo Surface Primer beforehand, letting it dry 24 hours. Sand lightly between coats with fine-grit sandpaper, wipe clean with a damp cloth.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Eduard PE Masks
tips.text: Soak Eduard PE masks in warm water for 15-20 seconds until soft. Apply soap solution to the model, then gently lay masks in place. Gently pat dry with a tissue. Spray Vallejo Air paint, letting each coat dry for 5 minutes. Carefully peel off masks immediately after painting, using tweezers if needed.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes
tips.text: Shake AK Interactive Wash bottles well before use. Apply thin coats, focusing on recesses, using a soft brush or dropper bottle. Let dry 10-15 minutes. Remove excess with a damp cloth. For panel line washing, use a fine brush, applying wash along panel lines. Seal with Vallejo Acrylic Gloss Varnish before weathering.

tips.title: Chipping with Sponges — Tamiya Weathering Master Set
tips.text: Dab Tamiya Weathering Master Set chipping colors onto a damp sponge. Gently pat onto the model, focusing on edges and high-wear areas. Let dry 10 minutes. Carefully remove excess with a damp cloth. Seal with Vallejo Acrylic Matt Varnish before applying further weathering effects.
